name: std::allocator_traits<Alloc>::destroy

declarations.code:
template <class T>

static void destroy(Alloc &a, T *p);

intro: Calls the destructor of the object pointed to by p. If possible, does so by calling a.destroy(p). If not possible (e.g. Alloc does not have the member function destroy()), then calls the destructor of *p directly, as p->~T()(until C++20)std::destroy_at(p)(since C++20).

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
a

 -

 allocator to use for destruction


 p

 -

 pointer to the object being destroyed

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: Because this function provides the automatic fall back to direct call to the destructor, the member function destroy() is an optional Allocator requirement since C++11.
